decisions.title: WCAG Level Target
decisions.summary: The project targets WCAG Level AA for accessibility, with a goal to achieve AAA for critical features.

decisions.title: Screen Reader Announcement Hook
decisions.summary: A custom `useAnnouncement` hook is implemented to manage screen reader announcements for dynamic updates, allowing messages to be announced with 'polite' or 'assertive' priority.

decisions.title: Screen Reader Only Text Utility
decisions.summary: A `.sr-only` CSS class is provided to visually hide elements while keeping them accessible to screen readers, used for elements like icon-only buttons.

decisions.title: Motion Preference Respect
decisions.summary: The application respects the user's `prefers-reduced-motion` media query preference, disabling or reducing animations for users who prefer less motion.

decisions.title: Automated Accessibility Testing Tools
decisions.summary: Automated accessibility testing is integrated using `@axe-core/react` and `jest-axe` to ensure components meet accessibility standards.

decisions.title: Component Library Naming
decisions.summary: The component library is named 'CryptoVault UI'.

decisions.title: Atomic Design Structure
decisions.summary: The component library follows an Atomic Design structure, categorizing components into Atoms, Molecules, and Organisms.

decisions.title: Classname Utility for Tailwind
decisions.summary: The `cn` utility from `@/utils/classnames` is used for concatenating and merging Tailwind CSS classes, ensuring proper class resolution.

decisions.title: Input Component Ref Forwarding
decisions.summary: The `Input` component uses `forwardRef` to allow parent components to directly access the underlying DOM input element.

decisions.title: Utility Functions for Formatting
decisions.summary: A set of utility functions (`formatCurrency`, `formatCrypto`, `formatPercent`, `formatNumber`) are provided in `src/utils/format.ts` for consistent data presentation.

decisions.title: Date Formatting Library
decisions.summary: The `date-fns` library is used for all date and time formatting operations, providing functions like `formatDate`, `formatDateTime`, and `formatRelativeTime`.

decisions.title: Form State Management Library
decisions.summary: React Hook Form is chosen for managing form state due to its performance benefits (minimal re-renders) and robust features.

decisions.title: Schema Validation Library
decisions.summary: Zod is used for schema validation, providing type-safe validation and clear error messages.

decisions.title: Form Validation UX Pattern
decisions.summary: The chosen UX pattern for form validation is inline validation with helpful messages, providing immediate feedback to the user.

decisions.title: Form Validation Mode
decisions.summary: Forms are configured to validate `onBlur` initially and then re-validate `onChange` after the first blur, balancing immediate feedback with performance.

decisions.title: Server-Side Validation Error Handling
decisions.summary: Server-side validation errors are handled by using `setError` from React Hook Form to attach specific error messages to relevant fields (e.g., 'EMAIL_EXISTS').

decisions.title: Generic Error Toast for Form Submission
decisions.summary: A generic error toast is displayed for form submission failures that are not specific field validation errors.

decisions.title: Password Strength Indicator
decisions.summary: A `PasswordRequirement` component is used to provide a visual strength indicator for password fields, showing which criteria are met.

decisions.title: Auto-fill Price in Transaction Form
decisions.summary: The `AddTransactionForm` automatically fetches and fills the `price` field with the current market price when a cryptocurrency `symbol` is selected.

decisions.title: Async Email Availability Validation
decisions.summary: An asynchronous validation rule is implemented for email fields to check email availability against the backend API.

decisions.title: Error Display Patterns
decisions.summary: The application uses field-level errors (inline below the field), form-level errors (at the top of the form), and toast notifications for different types of error feedback.

decisions.title: Toast Notification Library
decisions.summary: The `react-hot-toast` library is used for displaying toast notifications for success, error, and custom messages.

decisions.title: Frontend Framework
decisions.summary: The frontend is built using React 18.2 with TypeScript 5.3.

decisions.title: Frontend Styling Framework
decisions.summary: Tailwind CSS 3.4 is used for all frontend styling.

decisions.title: Frontend State Management
decisions.summary: Redux Toolkit is used for frontend state management.

decisions.title: Frontend Routing Library
decisions.summary: React Router v6 is used for frontend routing.

decisions.title: Frontend Build Tool
decisions.summary: Vite 5.0 is used as the frontend build tool.

decisions.title: Backend Framework
decisions.summary: FastAPI (Python 3.11) is used as the backend framework.

decisions.title: Database System
decisions.summary: PostgreSQL 15 is used as the primary database.

decisions.title: Caching System
decisions.summary: Redis 7.2 is used for caching.

decisions.title: Authentication Mechanism
decisions.summary: JWT + OAuth2 are used for authentication.

decisions.title: Brand Color Palette
decisions.summary: The brand uses a Deep Purple (`#6B21A8`) as the primary color, with light and dark variants. Emerald (`#10B981`) is used for gains, Red (`#EF4444`) for losses, and Gray (`#6B7280`) for neutral elements. Backgrounds are dark (`#111827`, `#1F2937`).

decisions.title: Font Family
decisions.summary: The primary font family for the UI is 'Inter', with 'system-ui' and 'sans-serif' as fallbacks.

decisions.title: Atomic Design Component Structure
decisions.summary: The component architecture follows Atomic Design principles, organizing components into `atoms`, `molecules`, `organisms`, `templates`, `pages`, and `features` directories.

decisions.title: Responsive Design Framework
decisions.summary: The responsive design system adopts a Mobile-First approach.

decisions.title: Tailwind CSS Breakpoints
decisions.summary: The project uses the default Tailwind CSS breakpoints for responsive design: `sm` (640px), `md` (768px), `lg` (1024px), `xl` (1280px), `2xl` (1536px).

decisions.title: Dashboard Layout Strategy
decisions.summary: The dashboard layout features a mobile header and a sidebar that is hidden on mobile and visible on desktop, with main content adjusting its padding accordingly.

decisions.title: Responsive Data Table Implementation
decisions.summary: Data tables are implemented with a responsive strategy: a full table view for desktop screens and a card-based view for mobile screens.

decisions.title: Responsive Modal Dialogs
decisions.summary: Modal dialogs are designed to appear as bottom sheets on mobile devices and as centered modals on desktop screens.

decisions.title: Responsive Typography Scale
decisions.summary: Heading and body text sizes are designed to scale with the viewport, using responsive Tailwind classes (e.g., `text-3xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl`).

decisions.title: Optimal Line Length for Readability
decisions.summary: Content is constrained to an optimal reading width of 60-75 characters on desktop (`sm:max-w-2xl`) while being full width on mobile.

decisions.title: Mobile Bottom Navigation
decisions.summary: A fixed bottom navigation bar is implemented for mobile devices, accounting for safe areas (e.g., iPhone notch) with `safe-area-inset-bottom`.

decisions.title: Responsive Image Handling
decisions.summary: Images are made responsive using `next/image` for automatic optimization or the `<picture>` element for art direction based on media queries.

decisions.title: Responsive Video Embeds
decisions.summary: Video embeds are wrapped in a responsive aspect ratio container (`aspect-video`) to maintain their proportions across different screen sizes.

decisions.title: Responsive Form Layouts
decisions.summary: Form layouts are designed to be stacked on mobile and side-by-side on desktop, with submit buttons adapting their width.

decisions.title: Lazy Loading for Performance
decisions.summary: Heavy components located below the fold are lazy-loaded using `React.lazy` and `Suspense` to improve initial page load performance.

decisions.title: Conditional Rendering for Performance
decisions.summary: Heavy components are conditionally rendered only on larger screens (e.g., desktop) to optimize performance for mobile devices.

decisions.title: Responsive Design Testing Strategy
decisions.summary: Responsive design is tested using browser DevTools with specific device viewport sizes and through component testing by mocking `window.matchMedia`.

decisions.title: TypeScript Strict Mode Enforcement
decisions.summary: TypeScript strict mode is fully enforced in the project's `tsconfig.json` to ensure type safety and catch common errors early.

decisions.title: Approved Libraries List
decisions.summary: A specific list of approved libraries is maintained for different categories (State, Forms, Charts, HTTP, Dates) to ensure consistency and quality.

decisions.title: Code Splitting Strategy
decisions.summary: Heavy components are lazy-loaded using `React.lazy` and `Suspense` to improve initial load times.

decisions.title: Memoization Strategy
decisions.summary: `useMemo` is used for expensive calculations and `useCallback` for event handlers passed to children to prevent unnecessary re-renders and optimize performance.

decisions.title: Input Validation Library
decisions.summary: Zod is used for input validation to ensure data integrity and security.

decisions.title: JWT Token Storage
decisions.summary: JWT tokens are stored exclusively in httpOnly cookies to mitigate XSS attacks.

decisions.title: Token Refresh Strategy
decisions.summary: A token refresh strategy is implemented to manage the lifecycle of JWT tokens.

decisions.title: Session Timeout
decisions.summary: User sessions have a 30-minute idle timeout.

decisions.title: Redux Toolkit + RTK Query for State Management
decisions.summary: The application uses Redux Toolkit for global state management and RTK Query for data fetching, caching, and synchronization.

decisions.title: Redux Store Structure
decisions.summary: The Redux store is configured with `auth`, `portfolio`, and `ui` slices, along with an `api` reducer from RTK Query. Middleware includes `api.middleware`.

decisions.title: RTK Query Base URL
decisions.summary: The RTK Query API's base URL is configured to use `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL`, allowing for environment-specific API endpoints.

decisions.title: RTK Query Authentication Headers
decisions.summary: RTK Query's `prepareHeaders` function automatically adds a `Bearer` token from the Redux `auth` slice to all API requests.

decisions.title: RTK Query Cache Tag Types
decisions.summary: RTK Query uses `['Portfolio', 'Assets', 'Transactions']` as `tagTypes` for intelligent cache invalidation and re-fetching.

decisions.title: Market Price Polling Interval
decisions.summary: The `getMarketPrices` RTK Query endpoint is configured to poll for updates every 10 seconds.

decisions.title: Typed Redux Hooks
decisions.summary: Custom typed hooks (`useAppDispatch`, `useAppSelector`) are provided to ensure type safety when interacting with the Redux store.

decisions.title: Toast Notification Hook
decisions.summary: A `useToast` custom hook is implemented to simplify dispatching toast notifications (success, error, info) via the UI Redux slice.

decisions.title: WebSocket Integration for Real-time Price Updates
decisions.summary: The `PortfolioPage` integrates a WebSocket connection to `wss://api.cryptovault.com/ws/prices` to receive and dispatch real-time asset price updates to the Redux store.

decisions.title: Redux State Persistence
decisions.summary: A `persistenceMiddleware` is implemented to save specific Redux slices (`auth`, `ui`) to `localStorage` for state rehydration on app startup.

decisions.title: Redux DevTools Enabled
decisions.summary: Redux DevTools are enabled in development environments for easier state debugging and inspection.

decisions.title: Authentication System Objective
decisions.summary: The objective is to implement a secure, production-ready authentication system supporting JWT tokens, OAuth2 providers, and two-factor authentication.

decisions.title: Authentication Architecture Overview
decisions.summary: The authentication system architecture involves a React frontend, an API Gateway (FastAPI), an Auth API Service (FastAPI), PostgreSQL for user data, and Redis for session management.

decisions.title: Database Schema for Authentication
decisions.summary: The database schema includes `users`, `oauth_accounts`, and `refresh_tokens` tables with appropriate fields, primary keys, foreign keys, and indexes for authentication and session management.

decisions.title: Password Hashing Algorithm
decisions.summary: bcrypt is used for password hashing, providing industry-standard security with a configurable work factor.

decisions.title: Access Token Expiry
decisions.summary: JWT access tokens are configured with a 15-minute expiry to balance security and user experience.

decisions.title: Two-Factor Authentication Method
decisions.summary: TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) is chosen for two-factor authentication over SMS due to its enhanced security and independence from carrier services.

decisions.title: Session Storage Mechanism
decisions.summary: Redis is used for session storage, leveraging its fast lookups and automatic TTL expiry for efficient session management.

decisions.title: Security Measures Implemented
decisions.summary: Comprehensive security measures include a strong password policy, rate limiting on login attempts, HTTPS-only endpoints, CSRF protection (double-submit cookie), SQL injection prevention via ORM, and XSS prevention (input sanitization + CSP headers).

decisions.title: Dashboard UI Objective
decisions.summary: The objective is to build a comprehensive, real-time dashboard for cryptocurrency portfolio management with charts, analytics, and transaction history.

decisions.title: Dashboard Visual Design Theme
decisions.summary: The dashboard uses a dark mode theme with Deep Purple (#6B21A8) as the accent color and Inter font family.

decisions.title: Dashboard Layout System
decisions.summary: The dashboard employs a responsive grid system following a mobile-first approach.

decisions.title: Dashboard Chart Design
decisions.summary: Charts on the dashboard are interactive and animated visualizations.

decisions.title: Dashboard Accessibility Compliance
decisions.summary: The dashboard aims for WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for accessibility.

decisions.title: Dashboard Component Structure
decisions.summary: The `DashboardPage` orchestrates several sub-components including `DashboardHeader`, `PortfolioOverview`, `MarketTicker`, `AssetTable`, and `RecentTransactions`.

decisions.title: Real-time Price Updates for Dashboard
decisions.summary: The dashboard uses WebSocket for real-time price updates, subscribing to `priceUpdate` events from `WebSocketService`.

decisions.title: Total Value Card Animation
decisions.summary: The `TotalValueCard` animates value changes over a duration of 1 second to provide a smooth visual transition.

decisions.title: Asset Table Sorting
decisions.summary: The `AssetTable` allows sorting of assets by 'name', 'value', 'change24h', and 'holdings', with a default sort by 'value' in descending order.

decisions.title: Market Ticker Auto-Scroll
decisions.summary: The `MarketTicker` component implements an auto-scroll animation to continuously display real-time price updates.

decisions.title: Dashboard Design Tokens
decisions.summary: Specific design tokens are defined for colors (Deep Purple theme), spacing (card padding, grid gap, section margins), and typography (page title, card title, body, labels) to ensure visual consistency.

decisions.title: Virtualization for Large Lists
decisions.summary: For portfolios with 100+ assets, virtualization using `react-window` is implemented to optimize performance of large lists.

decisions.title: Debounced WebSocket Updates
decisions.summary: WebSocket updates are debounced to prevent overwhelming the UI with rapid price changes, improving performance and stability.

decisions.title: Memoized Chart Data
decisions.summary: Chart data is memoized using `useMemo` to avoid re-calculating expensive data transformations on every render, enhancing performance.

decisions.title: Dashboard Accessibility Features
decisions.summary: The dashboard incorporates keyboard navigation, screen reader support with ARIA labels, AAA color contrast (7:1 ratio), visible focus indicators, and respects the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query.

decisions.title: Dark Theme Only for Dashboard
decisions.summary: The dashboard is designed exclusively with a dark theme, based on the preference of crypto traders and to reduce development scope.

decisions.title: Chart Library Selection
decisions.summary: Recharts is chosen over Chart.js for dashboard visualizations due to its better TypeScript support and declarative API.

decisions.title: Real-time Update Mechanism
decisions.summary: WebSockets are used for real-time updates to achieve lower latency compared to traditional polling methods.

decisions.title: Table Virtualization Threshold
decisions.summary: Table virtualization is applied for asset lists exceeding 50 items to optimize performance.

decisions.title: WebSocket Real-Time Architecture
decisions.summary: Real-time price updates are delivered via WebSockets following an architecture where Exchange APIs feed into a Price Aggregation Service, which then uses Redis Pub/Sub to broadcast to a FastAPI WebSocket Server, and finally to React Frontend Clients.

decisions.title: WebSocket Connection Management
decisions.summary: A `ConnectionManager` class is implemented on the backend to handle active WebSocket connections, subscriptions to symbols, and broadcasting price updates.

decisions.title: Price Aggregation Service
decisions.summary: A `PriceAggregator` service is responsible for collecting and aggregating price data from multiple exchange WebSocket streams (Binance, Coinbase) and broadcasting them to connected clients.

decisions.title: Price Aggregator Startup
decisions.summary: The `PriceAggregator` is started as an asynchronous task on application startup (`@app.on_event("startup")`).

decisions.title: Frontend WebSocket Hook
decisions.summary: A `useWebSocket` hook is provided for the frontend to manage WebSocket connections, handle incoming price updates, and manage subscriptions/unsubscriptions, including automatic reconnection logic.

decisions.title: Backend Message Throttling
decisions.summary: A `ThrottledBroadcaster` is implemented on the backend to limit the frequency of WebSocket messages, buffering updates and broadcasting them at a controlled interval (default 100ms) to prevent overwhelming clients.

decisions.title: WebSocket Connection Health Checks
decisions.summary: A heartbeat mechanism is implemented to send periodic pings to WebSocket clients, helping detect and clean up dead connections.

decisions.title: Frontend Debouncing for Price Updates
decisions.summary: A `useDebouncedPrice` hook is provided on the frontend to debounce rapid price updates before they are reflected in the UI, improving performance and reducing visual flicker.

decisions.title: WebSocket Monitoring Metrics
decisions.summary: Prometheus client metrics (Counter, Gauge, Histogram) are used to track WebSocket performance, including active connections, messages sent, and message delivery latency.

decisions.title: API Versioning Strategy
decisions.summary: CryptoVault uses URL path versioning for API versioning to ensure clear version visibility in URLs, easy routing and middleware application, browser-friendliness (no custom headers needed), and explicit version requirements from clients.

decisions.title: FastAPI Application Structure for Versioning
decisions.summary: The FastAPI application is structured with separate directories for each API version (v1, v2) containing their own routers, endpoints, and schemas. The main application (`api/main.py`) mounts these versioned routers with specific prefixes (`/v1`, `/v2`) and tags.

decisions.title: CORS Policy
decisions.summary: The FastAPI application includes CORSMiddleware, allowing requests from 'https://cryptovault.com' with credentials, all methods, and all headers. This ensures secure cross-origin communication for the frontend.

decisions.title: API Root Endpoint for Version Information
decisions.summary: The root endpoint (`/`) of the FastAPI application provides a service overview and status information for all API versions, including deprecation status, sunset dates, and documentation links.

decisions.title: Deprecation Strategy with Middleware and Headers
decisions.summary: A `DeprecationMiddleware` is implemented to add specific HTTP headers (`Deprecation`, `Sunset`, `Link`, `X-API-Warn`) to responses for deprecated API versions (e.g., `/v1`). This explicitly informs clients about upcoming sunset dates and migration paths.

decisions.title: Separate API Documentation for Each Version
decisions.summary: Each API version (v1, v2) has its own APIRouter configured with a prefix and tags, allowing FastAPI to generate separate OpenAPI documentation accessible at version-specific paths (e.g., `/v1/docs`, `/v2/docs`). V1's router is explicitly marked as deprecated.

decisions.title: Monitoring API Version Usage with Prometheus
decisions.summary: A `VersionAnalyticsMiddleware` is implemented to track API requests using Prometheus counters, categorizing them by version, endpoint, and status. This allows monitoring of migration progress and overall version usage.

decisions.title: Background Job Processing with Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL
decisions.summary: CryptoVault uses Celery for asynchronous task processing to handle time-intensive operations without blocking API requests. Redis 7.2 serves as the message broker, and PostgreSQL is used as the result backend for Celery tasks. The Celery worker cluster consists of 4 nodes.

decisions.title: Dedicated Use Cases for Background Jobs
decisions.summary: Specific operations identified for asynchronous processing include price updates, portfolio rebalancing, email notifications, report generation, and data aggregation. This offloads heavy computations from the main API.

decisions.title: Celery Configuration for Performance and Reliability
decisions.summary: Celery is configured with JSON serialization, UTC timezone, late acknowledgements (`task_acks_late=True`), worker prefetch multiplier of 4, max tasks per child of 1000, default retry delay of 60 seconds, max retries of 3, and result expiration of 1 hour. It also uses task routing to dedicated queues and priority queues.

decisions.title: Periodic Task Scheduling with Celery Beat
decisions.summary: Celery Beat is used to schedule periodic tasks such as cryptocurrency price updates (every 30s), portfolio metrics calculation (every 5m), daily summary emails (9 AM UTC), old result cleanup (2 AM daily), and weekly report generation (Monday 10 AM). Each task is assigned to a specific queue and priority.

decisions.title: External API Calls in Tasks using httpx.AsyncClient
decisions.summary: The `fetch_all_prices` Celery task uses `httpx.AsyncClient` for making asynchronous HTTP requests to external APIs (e.g., CoinGecko) to fetch cryptocurrency prices. This ensures non-blocking I/O within the task.

decisions.title: Email Notifications with smtplib and Jinja2
decisions.summary: Email notification tasks (e.g., `send_transaction_email`) utilize `smtplib` for sending emails via an SMTP server (SendGrid) and `jinja2` for rendering HTML email templates, ensuring dynamic and formatted communication.

decisions.title: Report Generation with ReportLab and S3 Uploads
decisions.summary: The `generate_tax_report` task uses `reportlab` to create PDF documents for annual tax reports. These generated PDFs are then uploaded to an S3 bucket ('cryptovault-reports') using `boto3`, and a presigned URL is generated for temporary access.

decisions.title: FastAPI Integration for Triggering and Monitoring Celery Tasks
decisions.summary: FastAPI endpoints are provided to trigger Celery tasks (e.g., `create_tax_report`) and to check the status of ongoing tasks using `celery.result.AsyncResult`. This allows the frontend to initiate long-running operations and poll for their progress and results.

decisions.title: Celery Monitoring with Flower and Prometheus Metrics
decisions.summary: Flower is used as a real-time web dashboard for monitoring Celery tasks and workers. Additionally, Prometheus counters and histograms are integrated into tasks to track total tasks, status (success/failure), and duration, providing granular performance insights.

decisions.title: Input Validation with Pydantic
decisions.summary: Pydantic models are used for robust input validation in API endpoints, ensuring data integrity and preventing common vulnerabilities like SQL injection by sanitizing and validating user input.

decisions.title: Parameterized Queries with SQLAlchemy
decisions.summary: SQLAlchemy's ORM is used to construct parameterized queries, which inherently protect against SQL injection vulnerabilities by separating SQL code from user-provided data.

decisions.title: Eager Loading or DataLoader for N+1 Query Prevention
decisions.summary: To prevent N+1 query problems, the system employs eager loading (e.g., `include: { assets: true }` in ORMs) or DataLoader for batching related data requests, significantly reducing database roundtrips and improving performance.

decisions.title: Migration from SQLite to PostgreSQL
decisions.summary: CryptoVault successfully migrated its database from SQLite to PostgreSQL 15. The rationale included PostgreSQL's support for concurrent writes (MVCC), rich data types (JSONB, Arrays), built-in replication, virtually unlimited size, advanced query planner, and role-based access control, addressing limitations of SQLite.

decisions.title: Enhanced PostgreSQL Schema Design
decisions.summary: The new PostgreSQL schema incorporates UUIDs as primary keys with `gen_random_uuid()` defaults, `VARCHAR(255)` for strings, `NUMERIC(20,2)` for monetary values, `NUMERIC(20,8)` for quantities/prices, and `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` for timestamps. It includes new fields like `email_verified`, `last_login`, `profit_loss`, `profit_loss_percent`, and `current_price`. Computed columns (`value`, `profit_loss`) are `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` for efficiency.

decisions.title: Performance Indexes for PostgreSQL
decisions.summary: Several indexes were created on the PostgreSQL schema to improve query performance, including `idx_users_email`, `idx_users_created`, `idx_portfolios_user`, `idx_assets_portfolio`, `idx_assets_symbol`, and `idx_assets_value`.

decisions.title: Automated `updated_at` Triggers
decisions.summary: PostgreSQL triggers (`update_users_updated_at`, `update_portfolios_updated_at`, `update_assets_updated_at`) are implemented to automatically update the `updated_at` timestamp column on `users`, `portfolios`, and `assets` tables before each update, ensuring accurate modification tracking.

decisions.title: Asynchronous PostgreSQL Connection with asyncpg
decisions.summary: The data import script and validation script utilize `asyncpg` for connecting to PostgreSQL, enabling asynchronous database operations and efficient handling of connections, especially during bulk data transfers.

decisions.title: SQLAlchemy Connection Pooling for PostgreSQL
decisions.summary: The SQLAlchemy engine is configured with connection pooling parameters (`pool_size=20`, `max_overflow=10`, `pool_pre_ping=True`, `pool_recycle=3600`) to optimize database connection management, reduce overhead, and improve application responsiveness.

decisions.title: AWS Cloud Infrastructure for Production
decisions.summary: The production environment is hosted on AWS, utilizing Route 53 for DNS, CloudFront for CDN/WAF, ALB for load balancing, ECS Fargate for container orchestration, RDS for PostgreSQL, and ElastiCache for Redis. S3 is used for static content.

decisions.title: Multi-stage Docker Builds for Backend and Frontend
decisions.summary: Both backend and frontend applications use multi-stage Docker builds to optimize image size and build efficiency. The backend uses `python:3.11-slim` for both builder and runtime, while the frontend uses `node:18-alpine` for build and `nginx:alpine` for production serving.

decisions.title: Non-root User for Docker Containers
decisions.summary: Dockerfiles are configured to run applications as a non-root user (`appuser`) for enhanced security, minimizing potential attack surfaces within the container.

decisions.title: Docker Health Checks
decisions.summary: Both backend and frontend Docker images include `HEALTHCHECK` instructions. The backend checks `http://localhost:8000/health` and the frontend checks `http://localhost/health` to ensure containers are running and responsive.

decisions.title: Uvicorn Workers for Backend Performance
decisions.summary: The backend Docker container runs Uvicorn with 4 workers (`--workers 4`) to leverage multi-core CPUs and handle concurrent requests efficiently.

decisions.title: ECS Fargate for Backend Container Orchestration
decisions.summary: The backend is deployed on AWS ECS Fargate, configured with `awsvpc` network mode, `1024` CPU units, and `2048` MB memory. This provides serverless container management without needing to provision or manage EC2 instances.

decisions.title: AWS Secrets Manager for Sensitive Configuration
decisions.summary: Sensitive environment variables like `DATABASE_URL` and `JWT_SECRET` are managed via AWS Secrets Manager and injected into ECS task definitions, ensuring that secrets are not hardcoded or exposed in plain text.

decisions.title: Centralized Logging with AWS CloudWatch Logs
decisions.summary: ECS tasks are configured to use `awslogs` driver, sending application logs to a CloudWatch Logs group (`/ecs/cryptovault-backend`) for centralized collection, monitoring, and analysis.

decisions.title: GitHub Actions for CI/CD Pipeline
decisions.summary: A GitHub Actions workflow (`deploy.yml`) is used for continuous integration and deployment to production. It triggers on pushes to the `main` branch and includes steps for testing, security scanning, Docker image building/pushing to ECR, ECS task definition updates, ECS service deployment, S3 frontend deployment, and CloudFront cache invalidation.

decisions.title: Alembic for Database Migrations
decisions.summary: Alembic is used for managing database schema migrations. The `env.py` configuration ensures that all models are imported and migrations run in 'online' mode with type and server default comparisons.

decisions.title: CloudWatch Alarms for Monitoring Production Health
decisions.summary: CloudWatch alarms are configured to monitor critical metrics, such as high error rates (e.g., exceeding 1% for ECS services), and trigger alerts via SNS, ensuring proactive incident detection.

decisions.title: JSON Formatted Application Logging for CloudWatch Insights
decisions.summary: Application logs are formatted as JSON using a custom `JSONFormatter` to facilitate structured logging and efficient querying/analysis with CloudWatch Logs Insights.

decisions.title: FastAPI as Backend Framework
decisions.summary: FastAPI was chosen over Flask due to its native async/await support, automatic OpenAPI documentation, built-in data validation (Pydantic), better performance for I/O-bound operations, and comprehensive type hint support.

decisions.title: PostgreSQL as Primary Database
decisions.summary: PostgreSQL was selected over MongoDB because ACID compliance is critical for financial data, it supports complex relational queries for portfolio analytics, and it has a mature ecosystem and tooling with better transaction support.

decisions.title: Database Schema Design for Portfolio Management
decisions.summary: The database schema includes `portfolios`, `cryptocurrencies`, `assets`, and `transactions` tables. It uses UUIDs for primary keys, `NUMERIC(20,2)` for monetary values, `NUMERIC(20,8)` for quantities, `ON DELETE CASCADE` for foreign keys, and `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` for computed columns like `value` and `profit_loss`.

decisions.title: Performance Indexes for Portfolio Schema
decisions.summary: Indexes are created on `assets(portfolio_id)`, `assets(symbol)`, `transactions(asset_id)`, `transactions(timestamp DESC)`, and `cryptocurrencies(updated_at DESC)` to optimize query performance for portfolio-related data.

decisions.title: Automated Portfolio Value Update Trigger
decisions.summary: A PostgreSQL trigger `asset_value_changed` is implemented to automatically update `portfolios.total_value` and `updated_at` whenever an asset is inserted, updated, or deleted. This ensures portfolio totals are always current.

decisions.title: Integration with Multiple Cryptocurrency Exchanges
decisions.summary: The system integrates with Binance (REST API + WebSocket), Coinbase Pro (REST API), and Kraken (REST API) to fetch real-time prices, place orders, and manage account balances. `aiohttp` is used for asynchronous HTTP requests.

decisions.title: Redis Caching Strategy for Performance
decisions.summary: A Redis caching layer is implemented to store frequently accessed data with specific Time-To-Live (TTL) values: cryptocurrency prices (10s), user portfolios (30s), market data (60s), and user sessions (30m). This reduces database load and improves API response times.

decisions.title: Layered Architecture Pattern
decisions.summary: The CryptoVault backend follows a Layered Architecture pattern, separating concerns into distinct layers: API (Routers), Service (Business Logic), Repository (Data Access), and Model (Domain Entities). Communication flows from Request → Router → Service → Repository → Database.

decisions.title: RESTful HTTP and WebSocket Communication
decisions.summary: The system primarily uses RESTful HTTP for API communication, complemented by WebSocket for real-time data updates, such as market prices or trading events.

decisions.title: Technology Stack Selection
decisions.summary: The core framework is Python 3.11+ with FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic. Database uses SQLAlchemy, asyncpg, Alembic. Caching/Queue uses Redis, Celery. External APIs use aiohttp, websockets, python-binance. Security relies on python-jose (JWT), passlib (bcrypt). Testing uses pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, httpx, faker.

decisions.title: High-Level System Architecture with CloudFlare and Nginx
decisions.summary: The high-level architecture includes CloudFlare for CDN/WAF, Nginx as a reverse proxy, multiple FastAPI instances, PostgreSQL (primary/replica), Redis Cache, Celery Workers, and RabbitMQ Queue. This provides a robust, scalable, and secure deployment.

decisions.title: Eager Loading in Repository Layer
decisions.summary: The `PortfolioRepository` uses `selectinload(Portfolio.assets)` to eagerly load related assets when fetching a portfolio by user ID. This optimizes database queries by fetching all necessary data in a single roundtrip, preventing N+1 issues.

decisions.title: JWT Authentication with Refresh Token Rotation
decisions.summary: Authentication is handled using JWT tokens with a short 15-minute expiry. Refresh token rotation is implemented to maintain user sessions securely without requiring frequent re-authentication.

decisions.title: Password Hashing with bcrypt
decisions.summary: User passwords are securely hashed using bcrypt with a cost factor of 12, providing strong protection against brute-force attacks.

decisions.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Resource-Level Permissions
decisions.summary: Authorization is implemented using Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and resource-level permissions, ensuring that users can only access resources and perform actions they are explicitly authorized for.

decisions.title: API Key Management for External Integrations
decisions.summary: A dedicated system for API key management is in place for external integrations, ensuring secure handling and rotation of credentials for third-party services.

decisions.title: Data Protection Measures
decisions.summary: Data protection is ensured through HTTPS-only communication (TLS 1.3), SQL injection prevention via parameterized queries, input validation using Pydantic models, rate limiting (100 req/min per user), and strict CORS policy enforcement.

decisions.title: Testing Pyramid Strategy
decisions.summary: The testing strategy follows a testing pyramid approach: 75% Unit Tests, 20% Integration Tests, and 5% End-to-End (E2E) Tests. This ensures comprehensive coverage with a focus on fast, isolated unit tests.

decisions.title: Backend Unit Testing with Pytest
decisions.summary: Backend unit tests are implemented using `pytest`, with mocked dependencies for services and repositories to ensure isolated testing of business logic. `pytest-asyncio` is used for testing asynchronous code.

decisions.title: Frontend Unit Testing with Jest and React Testing Library
decisions.summary: Frontend unit tests are written using Jest and React Testing Library to test UI components in isolation, focusing on rendering, user interaction, and applying correct styles.

decisions.title: API Integration Testing with httpx
decisions.summary: API integration tests are performed using `httpx` to test the interaction between different components of the backend, such as endpoints, services, and the database. These tests verify the correct functioning of critical API paths.

decisions.title: End-to-End Testing with Playwright
decisions.summary: End-to-End (E2E) tests are implemented using Playwright to simulate real user scenarios, covering the entire application flow from login to portfolio management and real-time updates, ensuring the system works as expected from a user's perspective.

decisions.title: Performance Testing with Locust
decisions.summary: Load testing is conducted using Locust to simulate multiple concurrent users interacting with the API, measuring response times and throughput under various load conditions to identify performance bottlenecks.

decisions.title: CI/CD Test Pipeline with GitHub Actions
decisions.summary: A dedicated CI/CD test pipeline is set up using GitHub Actions. It runs backend tests (pytest with coverage), frontend tests (npm test with coverage), and E2E tests (Playwright) on pushes and pull requests to `main` and `develop` branches, ensuring code quality and functionality before deployment.

decisions.title: API Protocol and Style
decisions.summary: The CryptoVault API adheres to RESTful principles, uses HTTPS only (TLS 1.3), and returns JSON responses for all endpoints. The base URL is `https://api.cryptovault.com`.

decisions.title: Authentication Mechanism
decisions.summary: The API uses secure JWT-based authentication (Bearer Token). All authenticated endpoints require a JWT token in the Authorization header. Access tokens expire after 15 minutes and can be refreshed using a refresh token.

decisions.title: Error Handling Standard
decisions.summary: All API errors follow the RFC 7807 Problem Details format, providing a consistent structure for error responses including type, title, status, detail, instance, and an optional 'errors' array for validation issues.

decisions.title: Pagination Strategy
decisions.summary: List endpoints support pagination using `limit` and `offset` query parameters. Responses include pagination metadata such as `total`, `limit`, `offset`, and `has_more`.

decisions.title: Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
decisions.summary: The target Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for CryptoVault systems is 4 hours, with a currently tested RTO of 3.2 hours.

decisions.title: Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
decisions.summary: The target Recovery Point Objective (RPO) for CryptoVault systems is 15 minutes, with a currently achieved RPO of 12 minutes.

decisions.title: Data Retention Policy
decisions.summary: A data retention policy of 90 days is enforced for all backups.

decisions.title: Geographic Redundancy
decisions.summary: CryptoVault infrastructure and backups are geographically redundant across 3 AWS regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1.

decisions.title: PostgreSQL Backup Strategy
decisions.summary: PostgreSQL backups include continuous WAL archiving to S3, daily full backups (2 AM UTC, 30 days retention), every 4-hour incremental backups (7 days retention), and continuous point-in-time recovery via WAL archives. All backups are encrypted and stored in S3 Standard/Standard-IA.

decisions.title: Application Docker Image Backup
decisions.summary: Production Docker images (api, frontend, worker) are backed up daily at 3 AM UTC by pulling them and saving them as gzipped tar archives to an S3 bucket.

decisions.title: Configuration and Secrets Backup
decisions.summary: All AWS Secrets Manager secrets and critical environment configuration files (.env.production, docker-compose.yml, nginx.conf, celery_config.py) are backed up to S3 daily with AES256 server-side encryption.

decisions.title: Redis Backup Strategy
decisions.summary: Redis uses AOF (Append Only File) for better durability with `appendfsync everysec`. RDB snapshots are configured to save frequently (e.g., every 15 minutes if 1 key changed). A daily script triggers a `BGSAVE` and uploads the RDB file to S3.

decisions.title: Database Corruption Recovery Plan
decisions.summary: In case of database corruption, the recovery plan targets an RTO of 2 hours and RPO of 15 minutes. It involves identifying the latest valid backup, decrypting it, stopping the application, dropping/recreating the database, restoring from the dump, applying WAL archives for point-in-time recovery, and verifying data integrity before restarting the application.

decisions.title: AWS Region Failure Recovery Plan
decisions.summary: For a complete AWS region failure, the DR plan targets an RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 15 minutes. It involves activating the plan, failing over DNS to a backup region (eu-west-1), restoring the database from cross-region replicated backups, provisioning new infrastructure in the DR region using Terraform, deploying the application, and notifying users.

decisions.title: Ransomware Attack Recovery Plan
decisions.summary: In the event of a ransomware attack, the recovery plan targets an RTO of 6 hours and RPO of 4 hours (restoring from offline backup). Key steps include immediately isolating systems, identifying the attack vector, restoring from immutable S3 Glacier offline backups, building completely new infrastructure from scratch using Terraform, restoring data, rotating all credentials, and engaging a cybersecurity forensics team.

decisions.title: Automated Monthly Backup Restore Tests
decisions.summary: Automated backup restore tests are scheduled for the first Sunday of each month at 3 AM UTC. These tests involve retrieving the latest backup, decrypting it, restoring it to a temporary database, verifying data integrity with specific SQL queries, and sending notifications/alerts based on success or failure.

decisions.title: Backup Monitoring and Alerting
decisions.summary: Backup processes are continuously monitored, tracking metrics such as backup size, duration, success, and failure rates using Prometheus. A Grafana dashboard is used for visualization, and PagerDuty alerts are configured for backup failures.

decisions.title: DDoS Mitigation Strategy (Immediate)
decisions.summary: During a DDoS attack, immediate actions include enabling emergency rate limiting on affected endpoints, activating CloudFlare 'Under Attack' mode (adding JavaScript challenge and blocking malicious traffic), and implementing IP blocking via Nginx configuration.

decisions.title: DDoS Mitigation Strategy (Scaling)
decisions.summary: To handle DDoS attacks, scaling actions involve horizontally scaling ECS tasks (e.g., from 3 to 12) and increasing RDS read replicas to boost capacity and improve response times.

decisions.title: DDoS Mitigation Strategy (Advanced)
decisions.summary: Advanced DDoS mitigation includes deploying AWS WAF rules with rate-based statements (e.g., limit 2000 requests per IP) to block excessive traffic and implementing CAPTCHA (hCaptcha) for suspicious traffic on the frontend.

decisions.title: Post-DDoS Remediation: AWS WAF & Rate Limiting
decisions.summary: As a permanent remediation after a DDoS incident, AWS WAF with DDoS rules has been deployed, and rate limiting has been implemented on ALL API endpoints.

decisions.title: Post-DDoS Remediation: Database Connection Pool & CAPTCHA
decisions.summary: Following a DDoS attack, the database connection pool has been increased, and CAPTCHA has been added for high-risk endpoints as permanent remediations.

decisions.title: Short-term DDoS Remediation Roadmap
decisions.summary: Short-term (next 2 weeks) DDoS remediations include setting up AWS Shield Advanced, implementing auto-scaling triggers for traffic spikes, adding geographic rate limiting, creating DDoS simulation tests, and training the team on incident response.

decisions.title: Long-term DDoS Remediation Roadmap
decisions.summary: Long-term (next quarter) DDoS remediations include implementing a CDN for all static assets, deploying edge computing for API requests, adding an anomaly detection ML model, and conducting quarterly DDoS drills.

decisions.title: Overall Security Posture
decisions.summary: The overall security posture of the CryptoVault platform is rated as 'GOOD' based on a comprehensive penetration test.

decisions.title: JWT Token Expiration Enforcement
decisions.summary: JWT token expiration is now strictly enforced by validating the `exp` claim during token decoding (`options={"verify_exp": True}`). An additional check ensures the timestamp is not in the past, raising a 401 'Token expired' error.

decisions.title: Rate Limiting IP Source
decisions.summary: Rate limiting now reliably identifies the client IP by prioritizing Cloudflare's `CF-Connecting-IP` header, which is from a trusted proxy. A fallback to `request.client.host` is used if not available, preventing bypass via `X-Forwarded-For` header manipulation. An IP whitelist for known proxies (Cloudflare IPs) is also implemented.

decisions.title: Account Lockout for Failed Logins
decisions.summary: An account lockout mechanism has been implemented: after 5 failed login attempts, an account is locked for 30 minutes, preventing brute-force attacks.

decisions.title: Generic Error Messages in Production
decisions.summary: Error handling middleware has been implemented to log full error details internally but return only generic 'Internal server error' messages to clients in production environments, preventing information leakage. Detailed errors are reserved for dev/staging.

decisions.title: WebSocket Connection Rate Limiting
decisions.summary: A WebSocket connection limiter has been implemented to restrict the number of concurrent connections per IP address (e.g., max 10 connections per 5 minutes), mitigating DoS and resource exhaustion risks.

decisions.title: MFA Enforcement for Admin Panel
decisions.summary: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is now enforced for access to the admin panel. Admin users must have MFA enabled and their MFA verification expires after 1 hour, requiring re-verification.

decisions.title: CORS Origin Whitelisting by Environment
decisions.summary: CORS configuration has been hardened to use specific origin whitelists based on the environment (production, staging, development) instead of a wildcard (`*`), preventing cross-origin attacks. Wildcard is only allowed in development.

decisions.title: Strong Password Hashing
decisions.summary: Passwords are hashed using bcrypt with a cost factor of 12, ensuring strong protection against brute-force attacks.

decisions.title: SQL Injection Protection
decisions.summary: SQL injection attacks are prevented by using parameterized queries via SQLAlchemy ORM for all database interactions.

decisions.title: XSS Protection
decisions.summary: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks are mitigated through React's built-in escaping mechanisms and the implementation of Content Security Policy (CSP) headers.

decisions.title: HTTPS Everywhere
decisions.summary: All communication is enforced over HTTPS using TLS 1.3 and strong cipher suites, ensuring data in transit is encrypted and secure.

decisions.title: Secrets Management
decisions.summary: AWS Secrets Manager is used for storing and managing all application secrets, ensuring no hardcoded secrets exist in the codebase.

decisions.title: Input Validation
decisions.summary: All API inputs are rigorously validated using Pydantic models, ensuring data integrity and preventing common injection attacks.

decisions.title: CSRF Protection
decisions.summary: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks are prevented through the use of SameSite cookies and CSRF tokens on all state-changing operations.

decisions.title: Database Encryption at Rest
decisions.summary: All data stored in the database is encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption, protecting sensitive information from unauthorized access.

decisions.title: Regular Dependency Updates
decisions.summary: All project dependencies are kept up to date through automated Dependabot scans and updates, mitigating vulnerabilities from outdated components.

decisions.title: Immediate Security Actions Roadmap
decisions.summary: Immediate security actions (next sprint) include implementing a Web Application Firewall (WAF), setting up an intrusion detection system (IDS), completing penetration testing for the trading engine, and implementing code signing for deployments.

decisions.title: Short-Term Security Actions Roadmap
decisions.summary: Short-term security actions (next quarter) include security awareness training for the development team, launching a bug bounty program, conducting a third-party security audit, and performing disaster recovery drills.

decisions.title: Long-Term Security Actions Roadmap
decisions.summary: Long-term security actions (next year) include achieving SOC 2 Type II certification, ISO 27001 compliance, establishing a dedicated Security Operations Center (SOC), and implementing a Zero-Trust Network Architecture.

decisions.title: Overall API Response Time Target
decisions.summary: The overall average API response time target is less than 100ms, with a current average of 87ms.

decisions.title: Database Query Optimization Strategy
decisions.summary: Database query optimization involves using eager loading to prevent N+1 query problems and creating appropriate indexes (e.g., composite indexes on `asset_id, timestamp DESC` for transaction history) to improve query performance.

decisions.title: Multi-Layer Redis Caching Strategy
decisions.summary: A multi-layer Redis caching strategy is implemented with different Time-To-Live (TTL) values for various data types: Hot data (10 seconds TTL), Warm data (30 seconds TTL), and Cold data (5 minutes TTL). Cache hit rate is monitored.

decisions.title: Database Connection Pooling Configuration
decisions.summary: The database connection pool is configured with a `pool_size` of 20, `max_overflow` of 10, `pool_timeout` of 30 seconds, `pool_recycle` of 3600 seconds, and `pool_pre_ping` enabled to ensure connection health and prevent exhaustion under load.

decisions.title: Query Result Pagination for List Endpoints
decisions.summary: All list endpoints (e.g., trade history) implement query result pagination using `limit` and `offset` parameters. This reduces response size, improves response time, lowers memory usage, and enhances frontend rendering performance.

decisions.title: Asynchronous I/O for External API Calls
decisions.summary: External API calls (e.g., fetching prices from exchanges) are performed asynchronously using `asyncio.gather` to run requests concurrently. This significantly reduces total execution time by being limited by the slowest call rather than sequential execution.

decisions.title: Frontend Asset Optimization
decisions.summary: Frontend assets are optimized through code splitting (lazy loading components) to reduce initial bundle size and improve First Contentful Paint/Time to Interactive. Images are optimized by converting to WebP, using responsive sizes, and lazy loading with Intersection Observer.

decisions.title: WebSocket Price Update Throttling
decisions.summary: WebSocket price updates are throttled by buffering updates and flushing them in batches every 100ms. This significantly reduces the number of messages sent, client CPU usage, and network bandwidth, leading to a smoother user experience.

decisions.title: Q2 2026 Performance Optimization Roadmap
decisions.summary: The Q2 2026 performance roadmap includes implementing a CDN for static assets, adding full-text search with Elasticsearch, deploying database read replicas for scaling, and developing a GraphQL API for flexible queries.

decisions.title: Q3 2026 Performance Optimization Roadmap
decisions.summary: The Q3 2026 performance roadmap includes transitioning to a microservices architecture (splitting the trading engine), implementing an event-driven architecture with Kafka, enabling Kubernetes auto-scaling, and deploying edge computing for global latency reduction.

decisions.title: Q4 2026 Performance Optimization Roadmap
decisions.summary: The Q4 2026 performance roadmap includes implementing machine learning for query optimization, predictive caching based on user behavior, and database sharding for horizontal scaling.

decisions.title: Critical Finding: Insecure Private Key Storage Remediation
decisions.summary: Cryptocurrency wallet private keys are no longer stored as plain text. They are now encrypted using a key derived from the user's password and a unique salt (PBKDF2HMAC with SHA256, 100,000 iterations) via Fernet encryption. Additional mitigations include HSM integration for enterprise accounts, multi-signature wallet support, withdrawal confirmations via email/2FA, and daily withdrawal limits.

decisions.title: Critical Finding: SQL Injection Vulnerability Remediation
decisions.summary: SQL injection vulnerabilities have been resolved by using SQLAlchemy ORM for all database queries, which inherently uses parameterized queries. User input is type-validated by Pydantic models, and authorization checks are performed. Database users have read-only access to sensitive tables, and query logging is enabled for audit trails.

decisions.title: Critical Finding: JWT Secret in Git Remediation
decisions.summary: The JWT secret key is no longer hardcoded or committed to Git. It is now loaded securely from environment variables using Pydantic BaseSettings. Git history has been cleaned, a new cryptographically random JWT secret has been generated, all existing tokens invalidated, and users forced to re-authenticate.

decisions.title: High-Priority: Missing Rate Limiting Remediation
decisions.summary: Rate limiting has been implemented across API endpoints using `slowapi` and `get_remote_address` to prevent brute-force and denial-of-service attacks. Specific limits are applied per endpoint (e.g., 5/min for login, 100/min for portfolios, 10/min for trading orders, 1000/min for market prices).

decisions.title: High-Priority: Insufficient Input Validation Remediation
decisions.summary: Input validation for cryptocurrency addresses has been enhanced. A `CryptoAddress` validator class provides static methods to validate specific currency addresses (e.g., BTC, ETH) using regex and external libraries. Pydantic models now use a custom validator to ensure only valid addresses are stored.

decisions.title: High-Priority: CORS Misconfiguration Remediation
decisions.summary: CORS configuration has been corrected to whitelist specific origins (`settings.CORS_ORIGINS`) instead of allowing all (`*`), preventing cross-site attacks. Allowed methods and headers are explicitly defined, and `max_age` is set to 3600 seconds.

decisions.title: Medium-Priority: Weak Password Policy Remediation
decisions.summary: The password policy has been enhanced to require a minimum length of 12 characters, at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character. Passwords are also checked against a list of common passwords.

decisions.title: Medium-Priority: Missing Security Headers Remediation
decisions.summary: A `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` has been implemented to add essential security headers to all responses, including `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, and `Permissions-Policy` to prevent various web vulnerabilities.

decisions.title: OWASP Top 10 Compliance
decisions.summary: CryptoVault demonstrates strong compliance with most OWASP Top 10 (2021) risks, passing categories like Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, Security Misconfiguration, Vulnerable Components, Authentication Failures, and Logging/Monitoring. Partial compliance for Insecure Design (threat modeling needed) and Software/Data Integrity (code signing pending).

decisions.title: GDPR Compliance
decisions.summary: CryptoVault is GDPR compliant, implementing data minimization, right to access, right to erasure, data portability (JSON export), explicit consent management, breach notification via incident response plan, and privacy by design (encryption by default).
